diagnostic_evidence.quote: is not $\mathcal{O}(h^p)$ in smooth regions with nonzero updates

issues.failure_explanation: The defined indicator is normalized, so for smooth nonzero updates of size O(h), eta_j is a constant away from zero and s_j^n is a fixed positive constant, not O(h^p). The higher-order O(h^{p+1}) truncation difference is proved only under the extra assumption |s_j^n| <= C_s h^p. The abstract and introduction assert that the proposed normalized shut-off has the higher-order property, but the paper itself only proves O(h) for that implementation.

failure_location.quote: We show the local truncation error modification is higher-order in smooth regions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Revise the abstract, introduction, and conclusion to reserve the higher-order truncation modification for an unnormalized indicator satisfying |s_j^n| = O(h^p), and state that the normalized implementation has an O(h) truncation-error difference; or change the method definition to use that unnormalized indicator.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised higher-order local truncation modification for UM-SRD in smooth regions is not established for the method as defined; only the weaker O(h) perturbation, the same order as the base first-order scheme, is supported.
issues.title: Higher-order truncation claim does not apply to the normalized shut-off
issues.why_classification: A source-supported repair is a contained weakening or redefinition of the accuracy claim. It avoids new global proof architecture and preserves first-order accuracy, but it removes a substantive advertised higher-order modification.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
is always equal to one
whenever any cell in the neighborhood has a nonzero update

issues.failure_explanation: With epsilon > 0, eta_j = Delta U_max,j / (epsilon + Delta U_max,j). If 0 < Delta U_max,j << epsilon, eta_j is far from 1; for example, Delta U_max,j = epsilon gives eta_j = 1/2. Thus the asserted property, and the appendix claim that it is always equal to one whenever any update is nonzero, are false.

failure_location.quote:
and $\eta_j \approx 1$ whenever any cell in $M_j$
has a nonzero update.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the property with eta_j = 0 iff all updates are exactly zero and eta_j -> 1 as Delta U_max,j / epsilon -> infinity, or explicitly assume updates are much larger than epsilon; adjust the wording in cor:normalized-accuracy accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Claims that s_j^n is effectively the constant 1/(1+tau^p) whenever any update is present, and that the shut-off depends only on nonzeroness, are overextended to updates comparable with or smaller than the guard epsilon.
issues.title: Normalized indicator is not one for arbitrary nonzero updates
issues.why_classification: This is a local boundary-case correction in a definition and its dependent wording. The main TVD and first-order consistency conclusions do not require the stronger claim.

issues.failure_explanation: For non-integer p >= 1, the function eta^p is not C-infinity at eta = 0. For example, p = 3/2 has a second derivative that is unbounded at 0. The stated smoothness property therefore holds only under an additional restriction such as p being a positive integer (or a weaker smoothness class).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis p in N (or p a positive integer) or weaken the claim to the correct smoothness regularity at eta = 0.
issues.overall_effect: The design claim that the blending function is smooth for arbitrary p >= 1 is false; only the integer values actually used, or a weakened smoothness statement, are supported.
issues.title: Shut-off function claimed C-infinity for all p >= 1
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local parameter restriction or regularity weakening. The stability and convergence results in the source do not depend on C-infinity smoothness for non-integer p.

issues.failure_explanation: In the one-neighborhood 1D configuration, W_i = {j} for i in M_j, so the paper's conservation constraint forces w_{i,j} = 1. The proposition instead assumes a weight w_{-1,-1} = alpha for the same symbol w. Unless the alpha denotes a different weight set, the cited weighted-SRD operator violates the stated weight constraint, so the TVD result is not established for the conservative S_j used in UM-SRD.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Separate the Berger-Giuliani pre-merging weights from the redistribution partition-of-unity weights, or correct the 1D weights to satisfy sum_{j in W_i} w_{i,j} = 1 and re-prove or cite the TVD result for that operator.
issues.overall_effect: The TVD-SRD proposition, and downstream results that invoke it, rely on an SRD operator whose weights are not the same as the conservative weights defined by the method.
issues.title: TVD-SRD proposition uses weights incompatible with the stated conservation constraint
issues.why_classification: This is not a one-line typo: it requires resolving an incompatible weight notation and verifying the TVD result for the actual conservative operator. The fix is contained, but it is nontrivial.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Define $S_j$ as the composition of pre-merging followed by redistribution.
Neighborhood finite volume update on the merged mesh: $Q^{n,-1} \mapsto Q^n$.
This algorithm is conservative by construction, inherits the TVD property proved in Section~\ref{sec:analysis-1D} on the 1D model problem

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem composes pre-merging, a finite-volume update on the merged mesh, and blended redistribution. The definition and algorithm instead perform a finite-volume update on the original cut-cell mesh and then blend the resulting U^* with the SRD redistribution. Also, S_j is defined as pre-merging followed by redistribution, not as the pre-merging map to Q^{n,-1}, and Proposition TVD-SRD concludes TV for the full S_j output, not for the pre-merge output. Thus the proof establishes TVD for a premerged SRD staging, not for the written UM-SRD time step.

failure_location.quote: Pre-merge: apply $S_j$ to map $U^n$ to neighborhood averages $Q^{n,-1}$ (lifted to the original mesh). By Proposition~\ref{prop:TVD-SRD},

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the definition, theorem proof, and algorithm describe the same premerged staging (pre-merge U^n to Q^{n,-1}, FV update on the merged mesh, compute the indicator from that update, then blend), fixing the proof to cite the pre-merging TVD inequality; or provide a new TVD proof for the original-mesh FV plus blending under a dt/h <= 1.
issues.overall_effect: The TVD theorem and the algorithm's claim to inherit that TVD property are unreliable as written. The proven result does not cover the original-mesh finite-volume update plus blending under the advertised full-mesh CFL regime.
issues.title: TVD theorem proof analyzes a different time-staging than the defined/algorithmic UM-SRD
issues.why_classification: The source supports a contained repair by aligning the algorithm and proof with the already analyzed premerged operator. This preserves the main TVD result but changes the described time-staging and indicator computation, so it is more than a local typo.

issues.failure_explanation: The fraction (h V_{j-1} + alpha h V_j)/(h + alpha h) simplifies to (1/(1+alpha)) V_{j-1} + (alpha/(1+alpha)) V_j, not to (1-alpha) V_{j-1} + alpha V_j. The displayed equality is false for every alpha > 0; for alpha = 0.2 the correct coefficients are 5/6 and 1/6, not 4/5 and 2/5.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 1-alpha by 1/(1+alpha) and alpha by alpha/(1+alpha) in the neighborhood-average formulas and in the dependent steady-state statements.
issues.overall_effect: The proof's intermediate differences and the steady-state formulas in Proposition srd-steady and Corollary steady-accumulation use wrong weights. The O(h) bound in the local-consistency proof survives after correction, but the stated algebraic forms are false.
issues.title: Incorrect volume-weighted average coefficients in SRD averaging
issues.why_classification: This is a local algebra correction. The qualitative steady-state modification and the O(h) perturbation bounds remain true with the corrected volume weights.

issues.failure_explanation: For alpha < 1 and nu/alpha > 1, a small nonconstant difference delta = U_j^n - U_{j-1}^n is amplified by the upwind update at the small cell: U_j^* - U_{j-1}^* involves a factor of order nu/alpha. Thus the base scheme is not stable for nearly-static data merely because the fluxes are small; the stated mutual-exclusivity argument is invalid.

failure_location.quote:
since a nearly-static solution produces nearly-zero fluxes regardless of
the CFL number.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or replace the remark with a valid stability argument for the small-s regime, for example by proving stability of the premerged merged-mesh scheme under a dt/h <= 1, or restrict the claim to exactly steady or constant states.
issues.overall_effect: The remark's justification that UM-SRD cannot become unstable when s_j is small under a full-mesh timestep is unsupported. It does not prove stabilization of the written algorithm in the small-blending regime.
issues.title: Stability remark falsely asserts base-scheme stability for nearly-static data under violated CFL
issues.why_classification: The defect is local to a remark. If the main TVD theorem is repaired to match the actual method, this remark can be weakened or removed without changing the central formal guarantees.
